title: Platform service identity, task queue and admin base are not specified for the workflow platform
source: Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 §R4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 4, 8, 20, 23, 24 and 44; Ownership Map v1
description: Template and Rules §R4 defines short, schema, REST base, topic and task queue for the 19 services only, and the workflow platform has no row there, so the platform has no login, no rwb_* schema, no REST base, no Kafka topic and no task queue of its own. The story works with what the sources do state: the Temporal namespace rwb-recovery, the platform task queue `rwb-platform` (Ownership Map JOB-22 and Architecture v5 slide 44), the PLT-owned admin operation POST /admin/workflows/smoke (Ownership Map) and no schema or topic of its own, all as the working read of the assumption. The semantic version label of the kit and the codec key names in Key Vault are also not specified.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 4 (shared platform: Temporal, shared with ACE; every service has api + worker, schema, topic and task queue); slide 8 (Key Vault codec server, payload keys AES-GCM; Temporal shared, task queue per service); slide 20 (every service: own schema, its own task queue and its own Schedules; /health and /metrics for the platform); slide 23 (L3 workflow kit, a versioned library owned by the platform team, and the codec server on L1); slide 24 (one cluster, a namespace per workbench, a queue per service); slide 44 (JOB-21 stuck workflow scan and JOB-22 smoke workflow owned by platform); Template and Rules §R4 (19 service rows and no platform row); Ownership Map v1 (POST /admin/workflows/smoke, JOB-21 and JOB-22 all owned by PLT)
proposed: Fix the platform login, task queue, admin base and kit version label in the Wave 0 Service Catalog and record them in the Ownership Map

title: The platform identity and the SCB IT approved Temporal server and SDK release are not stated in any read source

title: The platform worker has no platform login, no task-queue row and no admin base in any read source, and no source gives the build-ID format or the codec key name
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R4, R7.1, R7.2, R9); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 20, 23, 24, 35, 41, 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 12, 27, 28, 31, 32); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api POST /admin/workflows/smoke owner PLT; jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 owner PLT); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 071 Temporal worker and SDK in the recovery module v1.md (sections 3, 4, 12, 13 and 14)
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.6 Schedules; 13 Solution plan
description: (a) Template and Rules R4 has 19 service rows and no platform row, so the shared platform has no schema, no login, no topic and no REST base; the worker therefore has no login of its own in any read source, and the smoke operation has no base under which to publish. (b) The Ownership Map gives POST /admin/workflows/smoke to PLT and gives JOB-21 and JOB-22 to PLT, and Architecture v5 slide 44 and the Batch and Scheduling Design place PlatformSmokeWorkflow on the task queue `rwb-platform` at 06:00, but no read source registers that queue in the naming table of R4, so the queue name is a working read and not a sourced value. (c) The legacy story states that the build ID comes from the pipeline and that the codec key is one per environment, but neither the build-ID format nor the Key Vault key name appears in any read source, and the codec metadata of the contract cannot be written without them. (d) The Temporal server and Java SDK release is a pin: the legacy story pins it to the release approved for RWB-E1-070 and the temporal design slides ask for 1.30 or later, but no read source is the approved version record, which sits in Environment and Deployment Design v4 and is outside this work package's read set.
evidence: Template and Rules R4: the 19-row service table with schema rwb_<name>, login per service, REST base /api/recovery/<short>/v1, topic rwb.<short>.events.v1 and task queue rwb-<short>, and no platform row; the only platform lines are the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 and the namespace rwb-recovery. Architecture v5 slide 20: every service from the service template with its own schema and queue, and gateway-bff as shared platform with sessions only. Slide 24: one task queue per service in namespace rwb-recovery, and no platform queue in the picture. Slide 44: JOB-21 stuck workflow scan every 5 minutes owner platform, JOB-22 smoke workflow 06:00 owner platform, mechanism Schedule. Ownership Map: POST /admin/workflows/smoke owner PLT with the ruling that Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-22 and the Batch and Scheduling Design run PlatformSmokeWorkflow on the platform queue; JOB-22 replacement 'Temporal Schedule platform smoke in rwb-platform (PLT), starts PlatformSmokeWorkflow'; no api row and no job row states a login, an admin base or a queue registration. RWB-E1-071 sections 3, 4 and 13: the build ID from the pipeline manifest, the Key Vault key name 'one per environment', the pinned SDK version and the parameter values temporal.namespace = rwb-recovery and temporal.taskqueue.platform = rwb-platform, all without a format, a name or an approved release record.
proposed: Fix the platform login, queue, admin base and codec key names in the Wave 0 Service Catalog and record them in the Ownership Map

title: The worker contract has no source for the admin base it publishes, for the platform queue row, for the codec key reference or for the build-ID format
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R4, R7.1, R7.2, R9); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 20, 23, 24, 35, 41, 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 12, 27, 28, 31, 32); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api POST /admin/workflows/smoke owner PLT; jobs JOB-21 and JOB-22 owner PLT); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 071 Temporal worker and SDK in the recovery module v1.md (sections 3, 4, 12, 13 and 14)
section: 3 Preconditions; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.1 REST operations provided; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: (a) The contract publishes POST /admin/workflows/smoke and its owner PLT from the Ownership Map, but no read source gives the base, the host or the login under which that path is served: R4 has no platform row and the edge contract leaves the public base at the gateway, so the operation is published with a path and no base. (b) The convention section publishes the task queue `rwb-platform` because JOB-22 places PlatformSmokeWorkflow there, but no read source registers the platform queue in the naming table, so the queue is a working read and a later Service Catalog row can change it. (c) The codec contract must declare a Key Vault key reference and a key version, and the legacy story names the key only as 'one per environment'; no read source gives a key name or a metadata field name, so the contract publishes the algorithm and the reference shape and leaves the name open. (d) The contract publishes the build-ID rule, and no read source gives the build-ID format. (e) The five error answers of the admin operation cite MSG-P4-001 and MSG-GEN-004, whose text is in no read source, so the document cites the identifiers and does not restate the text.
evidence: Ownership Map: POST /admin/workflows/smoke owner PLT, basis 'API Specification v4 (added in v4), x-module P3; Arch v5 slide 20 and slide 44 (platform jobs); Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-22 puts PlatformSmokeWorkflow on the platform queue', with no base and no login. Architecture v5 slide 44: JOB-22 smoke workflow 06:00 owner platform mechanism Schedule. Slide 11: the Temporal contract is a typed activity or workflow interface in a contract jar, with payloads through the codec (AES-GCM, keys in Key Vault) and no key name. Slide 23: payloads encrypted by the codec (AES-GCM) and workers pinned by Worker Versioning, with no build-ID format. Slide 24: the codec on every client and worker, with keys in Key Vault per namespace, and no key name. Template and Rules R4: 19 service rows and no platform row. RWB-E1-071 sections 12, 13 and 14: the admin operation with 401, 403, 404, 409 and 503, MSG-P3-036 and MSG-P3-032 stated in full, MSG-P4-001 and MSG-GEN-004 cited by identifier only, the build ID from the pipeline manifest and the codec key 'one per environment'.
proposed: Fix the platform login, queue, admin base and codec key names in the Wave 0 Service Catalog and record them in the Ownership Map

title: The platform identity behind the observability contract is not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 R4, R7.2 s12.8 and R9; ownership.json jobs JOB-21 and api GET /admin/scheduled-jobs; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 23 and 44; legacy RWB-E2-037 sections 3, 11 and 13
section: 1 Story; 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan
description: The contract can fix the metric names, the label sets, the three rules, the annotation, the query list and the map, but no read source names the platform identity that publishes and owns them: no platform login, no provisioning record for task queue `rwb-platform`, no admin base for the catalogue read and no published dashboard name. The contract therefore declares shapes and leaves the identity open.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20 gives every service the contract-first rule and the contract-test rule but names no platform contract owner; slide 23 makes the platform team the owner of L1 to L3 and names no identity; slide 44 gives JOB-21 to 'platform'; the Ownership Map has no platform row and gives the catalogue operation to P2 rwb-integration; legacy RWB-E2-037 declares the interfaces of the monitoring stack and the Temporal frontend and no owner identity.
proposed: Fix the platform login, queue, admin base and dashboard names in the Wave 0 Service Catalog and record them in the Ownership Map

title: The stuck workflow scan cadence conflicts: 15 minutes in the legacy story, 5 minutes in Architecture v5 and the Ownership Map
source: Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence and R9; legacy RWB-E2-037 section 4 step 3 and section 13; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 32; ownership.json jobs JOB-21
section: 2 Business rationale; 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 8 Business rule BR11; 12.6 Schedules
description: The legacy story runs StuckWorkflowScanner as a Quartz job every 15 minutes inside one process. Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-21 to the platform as a visibility query plus alert every 5 minutes, the Ownership Map repeats every 5 minutes with Temporal visibility, and the Temporal and Drools Design says the scan is a visibility query every 5 minutes by the platform team with jobs as Temporal Schedules and no Quartz. Two values and two mechanisms therefore disagree for the same job.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-037 section 4 step 3 'StuckWorkflowScanner (Quartz, every 15 minutes)' and section 13 component row 'Quartz, every 15 minutes'; Architecture v5 slide 44 row JOB-21 'Stuck workflow scan | every 5 min | platform | visibility query + alert'; ownership.json jobs JOB-21 'Temporal Schedule stuck workflow scan in rwb-platform (PLT) ... every 5 minutes, Temporal visibility'; Temporal and Drools Design slide 28 notes 'the stuck-workflow scan (JOB-21, a visibility query every 5 minutes, platform team)' and slide 32 item 6 'Temporal 1.30+, jobs as Schedules ... no Quartz'.
proposed: Keep 5 minutes as the target cadence and record the legacy 15 minutes as superseded
